subject.title: feat(gmail): add --inline and --text content modes to gmail attachment

question: Should core `gog gmail attachment` own PDF/HTML text extraction, or should this PR be narrowed to `--inline` and leave text extraction to a separately approved client/integration layer?
rationale: Both implementations appear technically sound, but only a maintainer can accept the long-term dependency, parser attack surface, support burden, and safety-profile contract for untrusted attachment parsing in core.

options.title: Split and land inline
options.body: Land `--inline` now as the direct remote-path solution and move `--text` plus the PDF dependency to a separate proposal with explicit trust-boundary approval.

options.title: Accept core extraction
options.body: Keep both flags and explicitly accept the isolated parser dependency after adding or confirming safety-profile and exact-command-allowlist proof.

options.title: Pause both modes
options.body: Leave the PR open or close it until the MCP/client contract for transporting attachment bytes and extracted content is defined more broadly.

recommendation.title: Split and land inline
recommendation.body: Land `--inline` now as the direct remote-path solution and move `--text` plus the PDF dependency to a separate proposal with explicit trust-boundary approval.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes core CLI scope and accepts a new parser security boundary, and release history makes steipete the strongest available owner signal.
